lesson_scope: Scalar and vector projections, foot of perpendicular from a point to a 3D line, perpendicular distance calculations, reflections across lines, point extensions along perpendiculars, and 3D geometric applications in pyramids and trajectories.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the formula for the scalar projection of $\mathbf{u}$ onto $\mathbf{v}$:
$$\text{comp}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{u} = \frac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}$$

Evaluate the scalar product $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}$:
$$\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 4(2) + 2(-1) + (-4)(2) = 8 - 2 - 8 = -2$$

Compute the magnitude of $\mathbf{v}$ and evaluate the projection:
$$|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-1)^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$
$$\text{comp}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{u} = \frac{-2}{3} = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Apply the vector projection formula:
$$\text{proj}_{\mathbf{d}}\mathbf{a} = \left(\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{d}}{|\mathbf{d}|^2}\right)\mathbf{d}$$

Compute the scalar product and squared magnitude:
$$\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 3(1) + 1(2) + 4(-2) = 3 + 2 - 8 = -3$$
$$|\mathbf{d}|^2 = 1^2 + 2^2 + (-2)^2 = 1 + 4 + 4 = 9$$

Evaluate the vector projection:
$$\text{proj}_{\mathbf{d}}\mathbf{a} = \frac{-3}{9}\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = -\frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1/3 \\ -2/3 \\ 2/3 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Foot of perpendicular parameter from origin.

hints: Express the position vector of a general point on the line: $\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 2+\lambda \\ 3+\lambda \\ -2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the position vector of point $F$ on the line in component form:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + \lambda \\ 3 + \lambda \\ -2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Impose the perpendicularity condition that $\vec{OF}$ is orthogonal to the direction vector $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OF} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 0$$
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2 + \lambda \\ 3 + \lambda \\ -2\lambda \end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = 0$$

Expand and solve the linear equation:
$$(2 + \lambda)(1) + (3 + \lambda)(1) + (-2\lambda)(-2) = 0$$
$$2 + \lambda + 3 + \lambda + 4\lambda = 0 \implies 5 + 6\lambda = 0 \implies \lambda = -\frac{5}{6}$$

Substitute the perpendicular parameter $\lambda = -\frac{5}{6}$ into $\vec{OF}$:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - \frac{5}{6} \\ 3 - \frac{5}{6} \\ -2\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7/6 \\ 13/6 \\ 10/6 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{6}\begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 13 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix}$$

Take the square root to obtain the exact distance:
$$OF = \frac{\sqrt{318}}{6} \approx 2.97$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Foot of perpendicular along coordinate line.

hints: Express a general point on the line: $\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1+\lambda \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the position vector of a general point $F$ on the line:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 + \lambda \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{PF}$ from point $P(1, 2, 3)$:
$$\vec{PF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - 1 \\ -1 + \lambda - 2 \\ 2 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 + \lambda \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Set the scalar product with direction $\mathbf{j} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ equal to zero:
$$\vec{PF} \cdot \mathbf{j} = 0 \implies -3 + \lambda = 0 \implies \lambda = 3$$
The coordinates of $F$ are $(1, -1 + 3, 2) = (1, 2, 2)$.

hints: The foot $F$ is the midpoint of $P$ and its reflection $P'$.

walkthrough.text:
Recall that when a point $P$ is reflected across a line with perpendicular foot $F$, $F$ is the midpoint of $P$ and $P'$:
$$\vec{OF} = \frac{\vec{OP} + \vec{OP'}}{2}$$

Rearrange to make $\vec{OP'}$ the subject:
$$\vec{OP'} = 2\vec{OF} - \vec{OP}$$

Substitute the given coordinates $\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OP'} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 - 4 \\ -2 - 1 \\ 0 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$
The coordinates of the reflected point are $(0, -3, -3)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Foot of perpendicular and exact distance calculation.

walkthrough.text:
Express the coordinates of a general point $F$ on line $l$:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 + \lambda \\ -2 + \lambda \\ 1 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{AF}$ from point $A(6, -3, 6)$:
$$\vec{AF} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 + \lambda - 6 \\ -2 + \lambda - (-3) \\ 1 + 2\lambda - 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + \lambda \\ 1 + \lambda \\ -5 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Set the scalar product with the line direction vector $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ equal to zero:
$$\vec{AF} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 1(-3 + \lambda) + 1(1 + \lambda) + 2(-5 + 2\lambda) = 0$$
$$-3 + \lambda + 1 + \lambda - 10 + 4\lambda = 0 \implies 6\lambda - 12 = 0 \implies \lambda = 2$$

Substitute $\lambda = 2$ to find the position vector of $F$:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 + 2 \\ -2 + 2 \\ 1 + 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluate the displacement vector $\vec{AF}$ using $\lambda = 2$:
$$\vec{AF} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + 2 \\ 1 + 2 \\ -5 + 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the magnitude of $\vec{AF}$:
$$AF = |\vec{AF}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 3^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9 + 1} = \sqrt{11}$$
Thus, the perpendicular distance is exactly $\sqrt{11}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Vector line equation and perpendicular distance from origin.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the direction vector of the line connecting $B(1, 1, 1)$ and $C(3, 2, 3)$:
$$\vec{BC} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 1 \\ 2 - 1 \\ 3 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

State the vector equation of the line using base point $B$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular distance from origin to line.

walkthrough.text:
Express the coordinates of point $P$ on the line:
$$\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2\lambda \\ 1 + \lambda \\ 1 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Set the scalar product with direction vector $\vec{BC} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ equal to zero:
$$\vec{OP} \cdot \vec{BC} = 2(1 + 2\lambda) + 1(1 + \lambda) + 2(1 + 2\lambda) = 0$$
$$2 + 4\lambda + 1 + \lambda + 2 + 4\lambda = 0 \implies 5 + 9\lambda = 0 \implies \lambda = -\frac{5}{9}$$

Substitute $\lambda = -\frac{5}{9}$ into $\vec{OP}$:
$$\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - \frac{10}{9} \\ 1 - \frac{5}{9} \\ 1 - \frac{10}{9} \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1/9 \\ 4/9 \\ -1/9 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{9}\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 4 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the exact length $OP$:
$$OP = |\vec{OP}| = \frac{1}{9}\sqrt{(-1)^2 + 4^2 + (-1)^2} = \frac{1}{9}\sqrt{1 + 16 + 1} = \frac{\sqrt{18}}{9} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{9} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: General line parameter solving and decimal distance evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Express the coordinates of a general point $Q$ on line $l$:
$$\vec{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + \mu \\ 2 + 2\mu \\ 3 + 3\mu \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{PQ}$ from $P(1, -2, -1)$:
$$\vec{PQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + \mu - 1 \\ 2 + 2\mu - (-2) \\ 3 + 3\mu - (-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \mu \\ 4 + 2\mu \\ 4 + 3\mu \end{pmatrix}$$

Impose the condition that $\vec{PQ}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{PQ} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 1(1 + \mu) + 2(4 + 2\mu) + 3(4 + 3\mu) = 0$$
$$1 + \mu + 8 + 4\mu + 12 + 9\mu = 0 \implies 21 + 14\mu = 0 \implies \mu = -\frac{21}{14} = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Substitute $\mu = -\frac{3}{2} = -1.5$ into $\vec{PQ}$:
$$\vec{PQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - 1.5 \\ 4 + 2(-1.5) \\ 4 + 3(-1.5) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -0.5 \\ 1 \\ -0.5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the magnitude of $\vec{PQ}$:
$$PQ = |\vec{PQ}| = \sqrt{(-0.5)^2 + 1^2 + (-0.5)^2} = \sqrt{0.25 + 1 + 0.25} = \sqrt{1.5}$$

Evaluate and round to 2 decimal places:
$$PQ = \sqrt{1.5} \approx 1.22$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Foot of perpendicular and ratio point extension.

walkthrough.text:
Express the coordinates of a general point $Q$ on line $m$:
$$\vec{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2\mu \\ 2 - 3\mu \\ 3 + \mu \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{PQ}$ from point $P(4, 7, -2)$:
$$\vec{PQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2\mu - 4 \\ 2 - 3\mu - 7 \\ 3 + \mu - (-2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + 2\mu \\ -5 - 3\mu \\ 5 + \mu \end{pmatrix}$$

Impose the condition that $\vec{PQ}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{PQ} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 2(-3 + 2\mu) - 3(-5 - 3\mu) + 1(5 + \mu) = 0$$
$$-6 + 4\mu + 15 + 9\mu + 5 + \mu = 0 \implies 14 + 14\mu = 0 \implies \mu = -1$$

Substitute $\mu = -1$ to evaluate $\vec{OQ}$ and $\vec{PQ}$:
$$\vec{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - 2 \\ 2 + 3 \\ 3 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 5 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{PQ} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 - 2 \\ -5 + 3 \\ 5 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$$

parts.label: (b)
hints: Since $Q$ lies between $P$ and $R$ with $PQ : QR = 2 : 3$, $PR = \frac{5}{2}PQ$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the vector ratio equation along the line through $P, Q,$ and $R$:
Because $Q$ lies between $P$ and $R$ with ratio $PQ : QR = 2 : 3$, the total displacement $\vec{PR}$ is:
$$\vec{PR} = \vec{PQ} + \vec{QR} = \vec{PQ} + \frac{3}{2}\vec{PQ} = \frac{5}{2}\vec{PQ}$$

Express the position vector of $R$:
$$\vec{OR} = \vec{OP} + \frac{5}{2}\vec{PQ}$$

Substitute $\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{PQ} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OR} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} + \frac{5}{2}\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -2 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 - 12.5 \\ 7 - 5 \\ -2 + 10 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -8.5 \\ 2 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -17/2 \\ 2 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Point reflection across 3D line and triangle area calculation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foot of perpendicular and exact surd distance.

walkthrough.text:
Express the coordinates of a general point $F$ on line $l$:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \lambda \\ 2\lambda \\ 2 - \lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{AF}$ from point $A(2, 4, 1)$:
$$\vec{AF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \lambda - 2 \\ 2\lambda - 4 \\ 2 - \lambda - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 + \lambda \\ -4 + 2\lambda \\ 1 - \lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Impose the condition that $\vec{AF}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{AF} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 1(-1 + \lambda) + 2(-4 + 2\lambda) - 1(1 - \lambda) = 0$$
$$-1 + \lambda - 8 + 4\lambda - 1 + \lambda = 0 \implies 6\lambda - 10 = 0 \implies \lambda = \frac{5}{3}$$

Evaluate the position vector $\vec{OF}$ and the exact distance $AF$:
$$\vec{OF} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 5/3 \\ 2(5/3) \\ 2 - 5/3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 8/3 \\ 10/3 \\ 1/3 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{AF} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 + 5/3 \\ -4 + 10/3 \\ 1 - 5/3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2/3 \\ -2/3 \\ -2/3 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{2}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$AF = |\vec{AF}| = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2 + (-1)^2} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$$

parts.label: (b)

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Point reflection and triangle area using perpendicular height.

hints: The base of $\triangle ABC$ is the segment $BC$ between $\lambda = 0$ and $\lambda = 2$: $\text{Base} = 2|\mathbf{d}| = 2\sqrt{1+4+1} = 2\sqrt{6}$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the position vector of the reflected point $A'$:
$$\vec{OA'} = 2\vec{OF} - \vec{OA} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 8/3 \\ 10/3 \\ 1/3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 16/3 - 2 \\ 20/3 - 4 \\ 2/3 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 10/3 \\ 8/3 \\ -1/3 \end{pmatrix}$$
The coordinates of $A'$ are $\left(\frac{10}{3}, \frac{8}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}\right)$.

Compute the base length $BC$ along line $l$:
Points $B$ and $C$ correspond to $\lambda = 0$ and $\lambda = 2$ on line $l$:
$$\vec{BC} = (2 - 0)\mathbf{d} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$BC = |\vec{BC}| = 2\sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = 2\sqrt{6}$$

Calculate the area of $\triangle ABC$ using the perpendicular altitude from $A$ to the line $BC$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Base} \times \text{Height} = \frac{1}{2} \times (2\sqrt{6}) \times \left(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{2\sqrt{18}}{3} = \frac{2(3\sqrt{2})}{3} = 2\sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Submarine trajectory closest approach and minimum distance calculation.

walkthrough.text:
Express the position vector of the submarine at time $t$:
$$\mathbf{p}(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2t \\ 2 + t \\ 2t \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector from sonar buoy $S(7, 2, 6)$ to the submarine:
$$\vec{SP}(t) = \mathbf{p}(t) - \mathbf{s} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2t - 7 \\ 2 + t - 2 \\ 2t - 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -6 + 2t \\ t \\ -6 + 2t \end{pmatrix}$$

Impose the closest approach condition that $\vec{SP}$ is perpendicular to the velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{SP} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 2(-6 + 2t) + 1(t) + 2(-6 + 2t) = 0$$
$$-12 + 4t + t - 12 + 4t = 0 \implies 9t - 24 = 0 \implies t = \frac{24}{9} = \frac{8}{3}$$

Evaluate the position of the submarine at $t = \frac{8}{3}$:
$$\mathbf{p}\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2(8/3) \\ 2 + 8/3 \\ 2(8/3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 19/3 \\ 14/3 \\ 16/3 \end{pmatrix}$$
The submarine coordinates at closest approach are $\left(\frac{19}{3}, \frac{14}{3}, \frac{16}{3}\right)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Minimum distance in exact surd form.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the displacement vector $\vec{SP}$ at $t = \frac{8}{3}$:
$$\vec{SP} = \begin{pmatrix} -6 + 2(8/3) \\ 8/3 \\ -6 + 2(8/3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2/3 \\ 8/3 \\ -2/3 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{2}{3}\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 4 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the magnitude of $\vec{SP}$:
$$|\vec{SP}| = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{(-1)^2 + 4^2 + (-1)^2} = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1 + 16 + 1} = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18}$$

Simplify the surd:
$$|\vec{SP}| = \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{2}) = 2\sqrt{2}$$
Thus, the minimum distance between the submarine and the buoy is exactly $2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Pyramid face median line, perpendicular drop from base center, and exact surd altitude.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Find midpoint $M$ of edge $AB$ with $A(0, 0, 0)$ and $B(4, 0, 0)$: $M = (2, 0, 0)$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the midpoint $M$ of the base edge $AB$ connecting $A(0, 0, 0)$ and $B(4, 0, 0)$:
$$\mathbf{m} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}) = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the direction vector of the median line from $M$ to apex $V(2, 2, 6)$:
$$\vec{MV} = \mathbf{v} - \mathbf{m} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 2 \\ 2 - 0 \\ 6 - 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

State the vector equation of the line $VM$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foot of perpendicular from base center to face median.

walkthrough.text:
Express the position vector of a general point $K$ on the line $VM$:
$$\vec{OK} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 + \lambda \\ 6 + 3\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Form the displacement vector $\vec{O'K}$ from the base center $O'(2, 2, 0)$:
$$\vec{O'K} = \vec{OK} - \vec{OO'} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 2 \\ 2 + \lambda - 2 \\ 6 + 3\lambda - 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \lambda \\ 6 + 3\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Set the scalar product with direction vector $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ equal to zero:
$$\vec{O'K} \cdot \mathbf{d} = 0(0) + 1(\lambda) + 3(6 + 3\lambda) = 0$$
$$\lambda + 18 + 9\lambda = 0 \implies 10\lambda + 18 = 0 \implies \lambda = -\frac{18}{10} = -\frac{9}{5} = -1.8$$

Substitute $\lambda = -\frac{9}{5}$ to find the position vector of $K$:
$$\vec{OK} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 - 9/5 \\ 6 + 3(-9/5) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1/5 \\ 3/5 \end{pmatrix}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular distance in simplified surd form.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the displacement vector $\vec{O'K}$ using $\lambda = -\frac{9}{5}$:
$$\vec{O'K} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -9/5 \\ 6 - 27/5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -9/5 \\ 3/5 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{3}{5}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the magnitude of $\vec{O'K}$:
$$|\vec{O'K}| = \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{0^2 + (-3)^2 + 1^2} = \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{0 + 9 + 1} = \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{5}$$

State the final result:
The exact perpendicular distance from the base center $O'$ to the face median line $VM$ is $\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{5} \approx 1.90$.
